title: g6lc_qemu conformance report
description: Where the configuration, the build manifest and the device tree disagree. This is the package's first-class output and is useful with no emulator attached: it answers, mechanically, whether a design's own three descriptions of itself agree.

schema_version.description: Bumped on any field rename or semantic change. Never reinterpret silently.

profile.description: g6lc-soc is byte-faithful to the design and is the only profile a diagnosis may cite. g6lc-virt adds virtio so an operating system can boot and is software-valid, hardware-invalid.

passes_strict.description: False when any row carries a verdict that --conform strict refuses.

evidence.description: Always false. Output of this package is a hypothesis and a checkpoint, never verification evidence.

oneOf.description: Enabled in configuration, compiled into the design, declared to software.
Enabled in configuration, but the compiled RTL is a stub. Refused under strict.
Live in the design but not advertised: the guest will not use it. Permitted with a warning.
Advertised to software but not live in the design: a guest-visible lie. Refused under strict.
A reader could not determine the value. Refused under strict; never silently defaulted.
Forced by a command-line override. Emulated, but taints every downstream artifact.

capability.description: Capability name, e.g. vector, hypervisor, instruction-supply.

also.description: Secondary observations. A stub row that is also overdeclared reports both, because they are two problems with two different fixes: the build manifest, and the device tree.
